title: string census verification run
note: Every structure and operation fact on string's census page as executable vectors; the border facts filed away there (parsing, printing, ordering, interpolation) are OUT of scope. Two reference texts carry the unit fracture: 'e-acute' U+00E9 (1 codepoint / 1 utf16 unit / 2 utf8 bytes) and the musical G-clef U+1D11E (1 / 2 / 4). Both are written as escapes wherever a language spells escapes conveniently, so no file encoding can influence a measurement.

expectation_alphabet.<any>: any result acceptable -- the language guarantees nothing here
expectation_alphabet.<raise:*>: must refuse at runtime, by any name
expectation_alphabet.<compile-error>: the build refused the program -- for F-s2 and F-s4 this is not a failure but the guarantee itself

language_status.csharp: blocked-deliberate (no toolchain in the container; not pursued)
language_status.swift: not run (bonus language, outside the census's 11 targets)

facts.description: A CONTENT comparison exists everywhere, spelling aside (==, .equals, eql). Probed with the language's own content comparison over a string built at run time, so no interning can answer it early.
Substring/slice by the language's OWN unit exists. Probed over ascii, where all three units coincide, so this checks that the operation exists and not which unit it counts.
A round trip through bytes with a NAMED encoding (utf-8) is exact, for text containing both reference characters.

What ONE POSITION holds -- the unit. Three camps: utf-16 code unit (java csharp kotlin typescript dart), byte (go rust php cpp), codepoint (python; the census does not place ruby, and this run does). Probed as the NUMERIC value of position 0 of each reference text. For 'e-acute' the codepoint and utf16 camps agree (233) and the byte camp says 195; for the musical-G-clef character the three separate cleanly: 119070 codepoint, 55348 utf16 (a high surrogate), 240 byte. The census does not place ruby among the three camps, so ruby's cell RECORDS rather than checks; its answer is carried into the log as a proposed census addition.

Whether a string can change IN PLACE. Immutable-value camp: python java csharp go kotlin dart typescript php. Mutable-object camp: ruby, cpp (std::string), rust (String grows in place; &str is the immutable view). Probe a is the one that matters -- two names on one string, edited through the first, read through the second -- and it is the shared-mutation question the census flags as the residue. Probe b is assignment into a position. Both live in their own programs because for several languages the answer is a REFUSAL at build time, which is itself the guarantee: rust's borrow checker forbids editing while a second name reads (probe a), and go, java, kotlin, dart and typescript have no position-assignment at all (probe b). php's expectation on probe b is the census's own placement of php in the immutable-value camp: the string does not change.

What `length` counts -- the F-s1 camps seen through one operation. 'e-acute' is 1 codepoint / 1 utf16 unit / 2 utf8 bytes; the musical G-clef is 1 / 2 / 4; the two together are 2 / 3 / 6. The census does not place ruby, so ruby's cell RECORDS rather than checks.

What indexing `s[i]` ANSWERS. A one-character string: python, ruby, php. A utf16 unit as a char: java csharp kotlin typescript; dart spells it codeUnitAt. A byte: go, cpp. REFUSED at the unit level: rust -- probe b does not compile, and probe c shows why, since a byte-range slice landing off a character boundary PANICS. Probe a is over ascii, so what varies is the SHAPE of the answer (a one-character string, or a unit number), not the character.

What the equality OPERATOR does, as distinct from a content comparison existing. `==` compares CONTENT: python go rust kotlin csharp ruby php dart typescript. `==` compares IDENTITY: java, where content is `.equals`. Probe a builds one side at run time so no interning can hide the difference; probe c compares a string with itself, where identity and content agree, and exists so that java's answer on probe a reads as a different question rather than a broken one.
